listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Saturday, November 7. Our top story is a change at the White House. Stephen Miller will replace Susie Wiles as chief of staff to President Trump. The change comes after sweeping Republican losses in the midterm elections. The report gives few details on the reasons behind the choice. Now the other front page stories. In Israel, the election was inconclusive. The center-right opposition has a chance to unseat Prime Minister Netanyahu. But the backing of Arab-led parties will be key. In markets, AI stocks climbed after trillions were wiped from market values. Investors had sold tech shares partly over concerns that the Democratic election victory would mean slower AI development. In Atlanta, Governor-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms announced her transition team. Georgia Democrats are preparing to run state government. She won by more than eight percentage points. And in football, the 49ers will have a healthy Nick Bosa for the first time since Week 2. Christian McCaffrey is also good to go against the Raiders. Now the sections. In tech, Anthropic is committing a portion of its shares to a new Public Benefit Fund. It is also expanding its partnership with the General Services Administration to bring Claude to all levels of government. In politics, Drop Site reports that recent U.S. strikes near Qeshm Island hit fishermen. The Lever reports that a billionaire-backed group of Democrats is blocking its reporters after they exposed its funding. In world news, Pope Leo has begun a twelve day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru. It is his first South American trip since lung cancer surgery. Paraguay's president, Santiago Peña, was impeached and is under house arrest after a banking crisis. In sports, the Rockets lost to the Timberwolves, one hundred seventeen to one hundred seven. Brandon Aiyuk met with the 49ers and says he is healthy and wants to be reinstated. In Atlanta, new visuals show MARTA's Five Points redevelopment, which is over budget and behind schedule. The zoning board also approved demolition of the Hardwick house despite a pending historic designation effort. In architecture, Chaos is bringing more AI into V-Ray and into Enscape. Alison Brooks Architects has completed the Cadence tower at King's Cross. In science, imaging of a 115-million-year-old dinosaur fossil points to blood cells, though some researchers are not convinced. Scientists also found a previously unknown baby right whale off Canada. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Stephen Miller will replace Susie Wiles as Trump's chief of staff
lead.note: Stephen Miller will replace Susie Wiles as chief of staff to President Trump. The report ties the change directly to the midterm elections, saying it comes after sweeping Republican losses. The chief of staff is the top aide who runs the White House for the president, so a change in that job is a notable shift at the center of the administration. The summary is brief and does not say why the president made the choice or what Miller plans to do in the role. The timing matters for the reader, because the midterm results have changed the political picture in Washington. Further details on the reasoning and on how the new arrangement will work have not yet been given in this item, so more reporting is likely to follow in the coming days.
